text:
The benchmark is frozen and delivered. Here's what I built and what the evidence actually supports.

## Deliverable

`/workspace/submission` (mirrored at `/workspace/suite`) — `run.py`, `evaluation.json`, `README.md`, question/grader assets, self-contained.

**108 distinct questions, 108 independently scored items, 3 frozen domain scores:**

| domain | n | families |
|---|---|---|
| coding | 22 | 8 spec-heavy Python implementations (12 hidden tests each), 4 numerical/scientific routines (6 property tests each), 8 code-semantics Q&A, 2 mutation-testing tasks |
| co-work | 28 | 13 AdvancedIF-style multi-constraint instruction-following, 15 GDPval-style occupational deliverables with inline source data |
| reasoning | 58 | 34 HLE text items, 14 ArXivMath-202606 problems, 10 author-written brute-force-verified probes |

Domain score = plain uniform-weight mean of observed item grades. No predictor, no fitted conversion, no clipping. Graders are deterministic local functions (subprocess test execution, constraint checklists, normalised exact match); the only model call in grading is a frozen `helper-simulator` equivalence judge for free-form reasoning answers.

## What the measurements showed

I got one full run (`development-01`, 102 items) and 10-item probes on `development-08`/`development-06`. Two findings drove real changes:

1. **Output truncation was the dominant artifact.** At 12000 tokens, dev-01 truncated 36/102 items — including 13 of 14 ArXivMath items — collapsing its measured ArXivMath score to 0.071 against a reference of 0.836. Budgets raised to 24000/16000/8000.
2. **Grader bugs found and fixed** via reference solutions and hand-written compliant answers: a wrong conservation law in the Crank–Nicolson test, a malformed character-class regex, a non-dangling "dangling escape" test, an ambiguous partial-structuring spec, and an `a.m.`-breaking sentence splitter.

On the 10 shared items across three models: co-work Pearson 0.913 (AdvancedIF) / 0.996 (GDPval); reasoning 0.445 (ArXivMath). **Coding was constant across all three models — undefined correlation, zero ranking utility on that probe.**

## Limitations I want to be explicit about

- **No cross-model domain scores or macro-Pearson were obtained.** Platform throughput (2 concurrent suites, 2 requests/model, ~75 min per 102-item pass) meant `development-12` never finished. The 10-item probe is far too small to iterate on. The suite was frozen on construct-validity grounds, not tuned to the visible labels.
- **Ceiling risk is the biggest open problem**: `code_qa`, `synth_reason` and `cowork_if` were saturated by dev-01. This is Pearson-neutral in principle (a constant offset doesn't change correlation) but compresses score gaps, and I had no time to re-measure after raising budgets.
- **The coding domain is structurally capped.** DeepSWE and SWE-bench-Multilingual rank these four models near-inversely, and SWE Atlas spans 1.1 points. A grid search puts the best attainable coding average Pearson at ≈ +0.31 for *any* measured score, bounding the macro objective near 0.77.
- $20.02 of the $100 development wallet used. A validation submission of the final directory was accepted by the gateway and then started running on `development-12`; it could not be cancelled and is still executing — its results are not part of this report.
